Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
232 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Benign weather continues through Wednesday morning with near to 
slightly above normal temperatures expected. Much needed rain 
chances arrive Thursday and Friday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Remaining dry and seasonable through Wednesday with rain 
  chances returning late week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Remaining dry and seasonable through Wednesday with 
rain chances returning late week.

Fair weather conditions are expected to continue through at least 
Wednesday morning as broad 1032-1034 mb high pressure meanders 
offshore. The surface high pressure system will sit off the Delmarva 
coast today before pushing further out into the western Atlantic 
Tuesday and Wednesday. Ridging will remain stationary over the 
region during this time with widespread subsidence and southerly 
return flow boosting temperatures above seasonable norms, especially 
during the Tuesday and Wednesday timeframe. Moisture advection will 
gradually increase tonight and again Tuesday night yielding the 
potential for patchy fog on both Tuesday and Wednesday mornings. 
Outside of the fog, no hazardous weather is expect until late week. 

Passing high clouds will remain prevalent today as a shortwave 
disturbance passes to the south. This will yield highs in the mid to 
upper 60s for most outside the southern Shenandoah Valley where 
temperatures will be slightly cooler due to cloud cover. Mostly 
sunny skies return Tuesday with highs in the upper 60s and low 70s. 
Mid 70s are expected Wednesday with incrsng clouds from the south 
and west given an incumbent trough of low pressure/cold front 
approaching from the Mid-South/Ohio River Valley. 

Much needed rain chances finally return Thursday into Friday as the 
surface ridge buckles and an incumbent upper level trough pushes 
east from the Great Lakes/Ohio River Valley. At the surface, is a 
wave of low pressure and cold front that will eject from the mid-
Mississippi River Valley into the central Appalachians Thursday and 
off the northern Delmarva/southern NJ coast Friday into Saturday. As 
a result, expect increased cloud cover Wednesday afternoon and 
evening with rain chances arriving from the west late Wednesday 
night into Thursday morning. Widespread showers are expected through 
Thursday with a potential squeegee line feature (i.e embedded t-
storms) Thursday afternoon and evening. The threat for severe 
weather appears to be low, but not zero. This will be something to 
monitor in the coming days given the track of the resultant surface 
low, presentation of the trough, and timing of the cold front as it 
passes through. Additional showers are possible Friday the front 
works east and a secondary wave of low pressure pushes along the 
coast. Rainfall amounts will range between 0.50-1.25" with locally 
higher totals along the mountains. Amounts have trended downward in 
the recent model runs with probabilities for an inch of rain 
areawide sitting less than 25 percent. Even with that said, any rain 
will be much needed given subtle drought expansion from our recent 
2+ week dry spell. 

Additional rain chances area possible Monday & Tuesday next week as 
a stronger cold front and area of low pressure move into the region. 
Temperatures will cool to more seasonable conditions as these fronts 
pass, with highs in the mid-60s and lows in the 40s at the start of 
next week. Conditions become drier towards the middle of next week 
as the trough transitions offshore.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected to continue through Wednesday 
evening with high pressure meandering nearby. Passing high clouds 
are expected today as a shortwave disturbance passes south of the 
region. Dry conditions will prevail with any showers/sprinkles 
remaining south of ROA/CHO/SHD this morning. Clouds will become 
scattered to broken tonight with pockets of patchy fog in the river 
valleys and at terminals close to the tidal Potomac/Chesapeake Bay. 
This leaves us with a narrow window for sub-VFR cigs/vsbys between 9-
13z Tuesday morning at terminals roughly from a line extending from 
PHL-BWI-DCA-RIC points east. Confidence in fog development is low 
given light onshore south/southeast flow. Better moisture advection 
arrives Tuesday night leading to higher probabilities for fog in 
these aforementioned locations. Outside of the fog, no significant 
impacts to aviation are expected heading into midweek. Winds will 
remain light out of the south/southeast today through Tuesday at 
less than 15 kts. 

Widespread sub-VFR conditions are increasingly likely Thursday and 
Friday as low pressure and a strong cold front push across the 
region. Periods of rain are expected both days leading to lowering 
cigs and vsbys. Winds will remain out of the south and southeast at 
less than 15 kts through Thursday. High pressure returns for the 
weekend with a stronger front and wave of low pressure early next 
week. 

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Wednesday morning. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast today through Wednesday 
as high pressure pushes offshore. By Wednesday evening into Thursday 
morning, expect the potential for southerly channeling due to the 
high offshore and incumbent trough from the Ohio River Valley. 
Confidence in this occurring is low with a focus over the open 
waters. 

Low pressure and a strong cold front will work across the waters 
Thursday into Friday. Widespread showers and perhaps a few 
thunderstorms are possible Thursday afternoon. Winds will remain near 
or just below SCA levels both days with gusts under 20 kts. High 
pressure returns into the upcoming weekend.
